title: Rens NOMAD : The All-in-1 Waterproof Coffee Shoe
subTitle:
After revolutionizing the everyday shoe with Rens 1.0 - Original Coffee Sneaker, we are back to give your favorite athletic shoes a run for their money. We’ve taken our signature sustainable coffee material and 100% waterproof protection and combined them with performance features to unlock your full athletic potential. 

The World runs on coffee. Now, so can you.
description:
NOMAD features our new AquaScreen™  3.0 technology. Along with our 100% waterproof guarantee, this new dedicated membrane is lighter, twice as breathable, and built for any activity.


Made from recycled plastic bottles, this new barrier offers you the freedom to run, hike and explore—in any weather conditions. 

Puddles beware.


NOMAD features our newest innovation, the SkyStep™ Performance Midsole. Precision air intakes placed at the heel and sole increase ventilation and breathability while maintaining total waterproof protection.


Specially engineered channels flush out hot air on the downstep, and pull in cool air on the way up. This creates a lighter sneaker with increased flex and more responsive cushioning.










ClimatePartner guarantees that all climate emissions of the product will be calculated, reduced and offset via recognized carbon offset projects.







After the release of the Rens 1.0 - Original Coffee Sneaker, we were amazed at all the photos we were getting from our backers. People were using their coffee sneakers for running, hiking, climbing, dancing, working out in the gym and so much more.

       We were ecstatic to see our sneaker used in so many different situations, and we immediately became inspired to build a shoe for all the active people in the Rens community.
 

So when we decided it was time to design a new sneaker, we went straight to the source: The People.


We brought in a stellar design team who used all of your feedback to create a sneaker with cutting-edge sustainable technologies and a slew of A+ features.












We are back, bigger and better than ever.

Headquartered in Helsinki, Finland, Rens is a group of diverse sneakerheads from 9 countries on 3 continents all united under a common cause: making the ultimate sustainable sneakers for the culture and our planet.











This campaign is promoted by Backercamp. Since 2012, Backercamp has helped 5,000+ creators make their projects a reality, raising over $325MM through crowdfunding.


braag - A boutique pre-launch to post-launch marketing agency leveraging data-driven customer acquisition to fuel record breaking Kickstarters.



More than $70,000,000 has been raised with Sprint's support.


Risks and challenges
We have poured our hearts into NOMAD and we believe that this is the next step in sustainable athletic sneakers that you can truly wear with pride. With your feedback and rigorous testing, we think you will love Rens 2.0 - NOMAD as much as we do.

Since our first campaign in 2019, we have spent 2 years diligently refining our production, logistics, and R&D processes for a greener and more efficient experience for you. In this time our partner network has grown to serve a global audience with warehouses on 3 continents. Our team has expanded from our 6 original members to a team of over 25 highly dedicated professionals.

The experience from our previous campaign and our direct-to-customer sales have readied us in uncountable ways to ensure that this campaign is a success. This experience, as well as the previous year for literally everyone, has also taught us that unique and unexpected challenges can arise with very little warning. We are more equipped than ever to deal with the challenges that can arise.

With all that being said, the models shown are still prototypes that have not yet advanced to the stage of production models. As NOMAD is still in development there may be slight changes in color, styling, or other details before full production begins.

Any changes, adjustments, or delays will be communicated to our backers with honesty and full transparency all along the way.

Learn about accountability on Kickstarter
Environmental commitments
Visit our Environmental Resources Center to learn how Kickstarter encourages sustainable practices.
Long-lasting design
NOMAD was designed with durability in mind. Our recycled upper capitalizes on the inherent durability of Recycled PET to create a material that can stand years of rugged use. Our all-natural outsole provides full coverage and long-lasting protection for the midsole. Our midsole is split in strategic flex zones to increase flexibility while also freeing it from typical wear and tear. NOMAD is a sneaker that can be proudly worn for years.

Sustainable materials
Rens 2.0 - NOMAD's 100% recycled upper is made from a 50/50 blend of recycled coffee yarn and recycled polyester constructed from 6 post-consumer plastic bottles.

NOMAD features an outsole that is made of natural rubber, locally sourced from our partner’s sustainable rubber farm.

The removable insole in every NOMAD features a 100% recycled polyester sockliner.

Every NOMAD contains a fully waterproof membrane made from 100% recycled plastic from post-consumer water bottles.

Sustainable Distribution
We will bulk ship rewards to regional warehouses for distribution to reduce the carbon footprint of last-mile shipping compared to having a centralized warehouse or shipping individual rewards via air-freight.

We will use 100% recycled and recyclable packaging including boxes, wrapping paper, and hangtags, etc.

We will minimize the use of printing on the shoebox to reduce the use of ink and reduce the weight of the shipment which ultimately reduces the carbon footprint.

Our manufacturing partners and the materials we will use are certified by recognized organizations and bodies such as GRS, FSC, and RCS.

Our manufacturing partner conducts various periodic audits (such as SMETA) to ensure they meet labor, health, and safety standards. The audit focuses on subjects such as management system and code implementation, responsible recruitment, entitlement to work and immigration, sub-contracting, and home working. This ensures that workers are fairly compensated, that no forced labor or child labor is used in the production processes, that the working condition is safe and fair.

We will not use any animal products or by-products; Rens 2.0 - NOMAD is a vegan product.

Something else
We have joined up with Climate Partner (https://www.climatepartner.com/en) to offset all climate emissions from production, packaging, distribution and shipping to a warehouse near you. With the Climate Neutral Product label, ClimatePartner guarantees that all climate emissions of the product will be calculated, reduced and offset via recognized and meaningful carbon offset projects. Together with YOU and our Kickstarter community, we are making Rens 2.0 - NOMAD the World’s 1st Crowdfunded Climate Neutral Sneaker.

title: Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game
subTitle: A strategic survival horror experience for 3–5 players. Become a Killer or fight for your life as a Survivor. Death is not an escape.
description:
Level 99 Games is a world-renowned publisher of tabletop board games and card games. Over 10 years, we've successfully launched and delivered over 20 Kickstarter Projects. We love Dead By Daylight, and we can't wait to bring it to life on your tabletop!


Behaviour Interactive is the developer of Dead By Daylight the video game, and we are grateful to them for granting us the opportunity to bring this horror classic to the tabletop.



BODA Games is our factory partner for this production. BODA has produced a number of games for us recently, including BattleCON: Unleashed, BattleCON: Devastation, BattleCON: Wanderers, Bullet♥︎, BlazBlue Exceed, and Shovel Knight Exceed.


Quillsilver Studio is a full-service tabletop games development studio with a combined 25 years of experience creating tabletop games. Quillsilver has helped over 40 campaigns reach their funding goal, and has raised nearly $6 million in crowdfunded projects.










Risks and challenges
Level 99 Games has run and delivered over 20 successful Kickstarter projects in our 10-year history. With each project, we learn new things to improve our processes.

Right now, the prototype of Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game is in the last stages of pre-production approval by our team and Behaviour™ Interactive. All that remains is to begin mass production, do a final approval pass on the factory copies, and ship.

Manufacturing, shipping, and delivering physical goods is a messy business, and there is always the possibility of delays or unforeseen obstacles—especially in recent years. However, we haven't encountered anything yet that we couldn't overcome.

Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game is our largest project ever, and will come with unique challenges in terms of logistics and delivery. With the help of our experienced, world-class distribution and localization partners, a factory we have worked with for over 5 years, and fulfillment centers that we know and trust around the world, we are confident that we can handle any obstacle that comes our way.

Our guarantee to you is as follows:
1. We will keep you updated monthly here on Kickstarter and on our blog with what's happening in production and delivery.
2. Your games will be delivered in satisfactory condition, or your money back.
3. At any time before the project ships, you can reach out to us for a full refund on your pledge.

Learn about accountability on Kickstarter
Environmental commitments
Visit our Environmental Resources Center to learn how Kickstarter encourages sustainable practices.
Long-lasting design
We designed Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game to be endlessly replayable, and with long-lasting parts and high-quality production and finishing. Your copy will last through hundreds of plays, and become a cherished collector's item.

Sustainable materials
We built Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game to have as small of an ecological footprint as possible, while delivering top-notch gameplay and replayability. Everything fits in the box, and everything is used—there are no inserts or expansion boxes to throw away once you get your game.

Environmentally friendly factories
Our factory partner, BODA, undergoes annual audits for environmental and social responsibility. You can learn more about BODA here: https://bodagames.com/

Sustainable Distribution
A lot of board game kickstarters come in giant boxes, with expansion after expansion. These needlessly bulky items and excess packaging have an enormous cost in terms of materials and fuel for transportation.

We designed Dead by Daylight™: The Board Game to be large enough to impress, but small enough to actually hit your table on a regular basis. The whole game fits in one box, and there's no more than there needs to be for the full experience. This ethos of simplicity makes the game less expensive to ship in terms of fuel and weight, and easier to store and play.

title: The postcard: Daily life
subTitle: Give yourself a reason to contact the person you love.
description:
From 2020 to 2022,  COVID-19  has made us experience a series of changes. We can't hung out with our friends or have a trip with family. People's feelings are often maintained through interaction, When lockdown, we are often not interested in contacting and talking with others.


so  I started thinking... ‘what can increase the fun of communicating with relatives and friends who are not around us？’


Even on normal days,  the desire to share is a little romance in life. Sometime the daily things we do also could be a interesting thing to share with your loved ones, and the postcard will be a very appropriate prop to achieve this.


These cards are printed on high quality matte paper, each card is themed with a daily activity. Your current situation or what you want to do with others. Finding happiness in the daily life is the theme of this set of postcard. At the same time, you can also enjoy the fun of handwritten letters.


With a postcard, in the ordinary daily life, let's give yourself a reason to contact the person you love！

title: Weeping Rocks: A feature length documentary
subTitle: revealing the urgency to save insect species through long-term scientific research
description:
Let’s take a look at those stretch goals in more detail:

$25,000 - Professional Sound Mix in a mixing theater. This is essentially a full-size movie theater with a sound mixing console in it: in other words, a filmmaker's DREAM!

$30,000 - Professional Color Grading for Weeping Rocks. The way a film looks can either make or break a project. In order to make the visuals of Weeping Rocks match the substance of the story, we will hire a veteran color grader to do the job right.

$35,000 - Stretch goal revealed at $25k

$40,000 - We can't wait to tell you what we have in mind! We can say this much, it involves seeing tens of thousands of butterflies in one place and getting some incredible footage!



Currently, we are in the middle of the sixth mass extinction—the sixth time in world history that many different species are declining at a rapid rate. The evidence is clear: the insect population faces global obliteration, and humanity needs to be prepared. 


Weeping Rocks is a feature-length documentary that focuses on the critical role small insects play in our fragile ecosystem, and the researchers who have quietly dedicated their lives to tracing, studying, and cultivating them.  


The film follows a UC Davis professor, Arthur 'Art' Shapiro, who is responsible for the largest dataset of butterfly populations in the Northern Hemisphere. For the past 50 years, he has been manually counting butterflies by walking the same trails in Northern California every week, and he estimates that he spends about 260 days out in the field each year.



A Monarch emerging from its chrysalis
Long term research is vital, because only from large amounts of data spanning decades can we come to more accurate conclusions about the effects of climate change. Art's work reveals the mistakes we’ve made and the drastic changes we have come to experience.  


Climate change is a complex issue that cannot be approached solely on an individual level.  Only through collaboration between many fields may we begin to understand our biggest challenges ahead, and begin to co-create possible solutions. 


The film shows the complex and diverse world of entomology, how future generations will carry on Art's research, and the interconnectedness of life on our planet.

“Love them or loathe them, we humans cannot survive without insects.”


Our subjects have spent decades working separately, albeit steadfastly, toward a uniform goal. From a scientist who has been counting butterflies for the past 50 years, to a farmer-owned cooperative that grows millions of beneficial insects per day, Weeping Rocks is an investigation of both the microscopic and macroscopic ramifications of climate change.


Professor Arthur Shapiro walking on one of his research paths (transects)
Arthur ‘Art’ Shapiro, a Professor of Evolution and Ecology at UC Davis, has been counting Monarch butterflies for the past half-century in the Sacramento area. By doing so, he has single-handedly created the longest butterfly monitoring project in the Northern Hemisphere. 


Lisa Gonzalez examines insects she has collected for research
Lisa Gonzalez, from the Entomology Department of the Los Angeles Natural History Museum, helps run a research project called BioScan, created by Dr. Brian Brown. BioScan seeks out ordinary people from Los Angeles to voluntarily donate parts of their backyards to science, in an effort to study and upkeep the city's fauna biodiversity. Throughout the course of this project, Gonzalez and her team have discovered a number of insects that were previously unknown, thus the city of Los Angeles is in fact a dry, subtropical paradise for wildlife.


Victor Perez inspecting and placing specimens
Victor Perez is the manager of a farmer-owned insect growing facility in Ventura County, CA. Perez immigrated to California from Mexico 20 years ago and started his career working for the spray division of Associates Insectary. Today, he manages the growth of beneficial insects for local farmers. Considered to be a greener, non-toxic alternative to pesticides, millions of beneficial insects are released by hand over thousands of acres of farmland.


Stephanie Turcotte at The Pacific Grove Monarch Butterfly Sanctuary
Stephanie Turcotte has been an educational docent for the Pacific Grove Natural History Museum since 2012. Stephanie is part of a team that counts overwintering Monarch butterfly populations every week at The Pacific Grove Monarch Butterfly Sanctuary. Thanks to volunteers like Stephanie, we know the overall trends of the Monarch butterfly population on the West Coast.


Insect populations are quietly disappearing before us, which will greatly impact the order of life as we know it.  Everything in nature is connected; everything is a chain reaction. Weeping Rocks will weave together the stories and life cycles of insects with the lives of those who study them.


It may seem insignificant to lose insect populations but they are the foundation of biodiversity.  We hope the message of our film will help to change the ongoing pattern of environmental destruction by extractive economies.


The 'Weeping Rocks' along the Yuba River in the Sierras with snowmelt water trickling down

Through the hard work of our team, this film has received the prestigious Allan Sekula Social Documentary Grant and is fiscally sponsored by Film Independent. We have also partnered with Save Our Monarchs Organization and Pacific Grove Natural History Museum.


Kārlis Bergs (Director, Co-Editor, Second Camera) is a Latvian born filmmaker based in Syracuse, NY. He received his MFA from California Institute of the Arts in 2020. He is the recipient of the prestigious Allan Sekula Social Documentary grant. He has shown films at Riga International Film Festival, Tacoma Film Festival, Jelly Film Festival and Black Hills Film Festival.  Bergs works to shed light on issues and subjects that may seem insignificant at first, but after further contemplation, are clearly crucial. 


Andrew Siedenburg (Co-Editor, Sound Mix, Post-Production Supervisor) is a New York based Artist, Filmmaker, and Sound Designer. He received his MFA from California Institute of the Arts in 2020, where he met Karlis Bergs and Jackii Chun. His work as a visual artist informs his interest in sound and vice versa. Andrew has worked on numerous short films and documentaries as editor, producer, sound mixer, and sound designer, and sees his work on films as part of his artistic practice. He is currently in the Whitney Museum of American Art’s Independent Study Program.


Jackii Chun (Producer) was born in Seoul, South Korea and raised up and down the Pacific Coast. She obtained her BA in Film Studies and Asian American Studies at UC Davis and went on to pursue her MFA in Film/Video at California Institute of the Arts. Her film, Space Ètude, No. 1, screened at REDCAT and was an Official Selection of the Blow-Up International Arthouse Filmfest Chicago in 2019. Father, her thesis film, was named a semi-finalist at the Flickers' Rhode Island International Film Festival in 2021.


This film is dedicated in loving memory of Alexey Kurbatov. 

Tragically, in January 2020, Alex passed away. This movie would not have been what it is without him, since a good portion of Weeping Rocks is Alex's camerawork. Alex's energy, positivity and curiosity was the driving force behind the shoots. Alex was not only an amazing cinematographer but more so he became my friend and mentor. 4 years ago, I didn't have any experience with working on documentaries, but he believed in the story and in me. Right from the start he was all in. This film has to be finished not only to cover the important topic of climate change and insect disappearance, but also to honor Alex's memory.


We have filmed Weeping Rocks on a shoestring budget, flying or driving up to Davis, CA to visit Professor Shapiro whenever we could save enough money to do so. This has allowed us to keep expenses low and maintain creative control during production.

However, we humbly ask for your financial help in the final stages of production and post-production. While our team has done everything to keep costs low and has worked without any financial reward, we need one last push to complete this film!

We have set a relatively low goal to ensure a successful Kickstarter campaign - $20,000, but ideally we need $30,000 to cover all the costs and to be able to compensate everyone involved.


We need your support for:

* 2-3x visits to Professor Shapiro and his colleagues

* Visits with other entomologists and scientists

* Editing costs for the film

* Sound mixing in a professional studio

* Color grading the film to polish it up

* Applying to film festivals


Without your contributions, it simply won't be possible for us to finish the film!!!





That’s right! YOU, yes you, can bring WEEPING ROCKS film to life!

There are two ways you can help.

1. Donate to our campaign right here on this page! Just click BACK THIS PROJECT and enter an amount. A contribution of any size, big or small is incredibly HELPFUL to us.

In exchange for your pledge, you can receive some super sweet, one-of-a-kind, WEEPING ROCKS REWARDS. For more info, check out our detailed incentive list!

2. If you can’t pledge that’s okay! Then tell everyone you know about this film! Follow us on Facebook. LIKE, SAVE, and SHARE our posts with your friends, family, and colleagues. Sharing this campaign is huge! Get on your social channels and SPREAD THE WORD!


We have included images of the physical rewards below. See the rewards column on the right for all reward options.

Special Digital ZINE ($50) 


Get a beautifully designed 80 page zine with extended interviews with scientists featured in the film. Over the years they have said so many interesting things, but sadly we can't include all of that in the film, otherwise it would be 5 hours long. This is your chance to see behind the scenes pictures and get to know their unique characters and fascinating thoughts on science, truth and the world around us.

You can ''Save Our Monarchs''! ($75)


We have partnered with Save Our Monarchs organization and we are offering to ship to your house organic Milkweed seeds ready to be planted in your garden this Spring, or gift them to your mom, who has a garden! Milkweed is an essential plant for many pollinators, but especially you would be helping Monarch butterflies. By getting this perk you are not only supporting our film, you are also helping Save Our Monarchs efforts. You also get everything else mentioned before.

Artist designed T-Shirt ''Pollinators Paradise'' (starting from $200)


A unique t-shirt designed by a fantastic artist Liza Stout! Not only you will support the film, but you will also provide exposures to the Monarchs where ever you go. Guaranteed to receive compliments and follow up questions about how amazing these insects are!

Limited Edition Framed Print ($500)


Get a unique 12x16 inches limited edition framed print from the film!

Risks and challenges
We have been working on this film for the past 4 years.
The biggest risk with this film is shared by all low budget filmmakers: our ability to finish what we started depends on the faith and support of our community. So, we hope that you will join us and help bring Weeping Rocks into the world!
